PROS

The pros of being part of a trading block are that you get more monetary influx. It's easier to trade across borders, and other trading blocks like trading with blocks.

In other words, the US is part of NAFTA, which prefers to trade with the entire EU instead of just Britain. Even though Britain is in the EU, trading directly with Brian provides trading "roadblocks" that you wouldn't see when trading with the EU, since there are multiple countries in the EU.

Think about it like you're an inventor, and you invent something. You can sell it to your local Walmart, and they'll sell it from that store, only... or you can sell it to the Walmart corporation, and they'll sell it in every store they own...

It's easy to see how a country can make money by being in a trade block. Other countries are more willing to buy/sell your exports, and you get to sell your stuff without border penalities and taxes. That are some of the pros of being in a trade block.

CONS

There are plenty of cons for being in a trade block... like the fact that jobs move across borders, not just goods. It's cheaper to hire a Mexican to do your job, and now that I can import the thing you're making, I don't have to make it in the US. So I'm not going t make it here, and sell it there... I'm going to make it there (for SUPER CHEAP) and ship it here for nearly free, thanks to the help of the trade block. This is one reason people don't like being in trade blocks.

Also, it opens your country up to having to listen to other countries. You don't like trading with your enemy? Well, we're part of this family/block, lo you need to get along! You don't want to let "refugees" into your country? Well, all of the EU decided that this is what we're doing, so you're going to be part of it. You want to use your own version of the dollar? Well, we're all moving to the Euro, because Greece is broke, and we're all in this together... so you moving to the Euro will hurt you a little, but we'll all help Greece.

Essentially, your country loses some freedom/sovereignty by entering a trade agreement.

BREXIT

These pros and cons are why Brexit voted. Some saw the benefits, and decided that they outweigh the cons. Some saw the cons and decided that nothing is worth those sacrifices. Everyone voted, and there was more that disagreed with the EU that there were that agreed.
